checks.outcome: The category with two parallel arrows satisfies both hypotheses and has a nontrivial automorphism of Sub(B). This refutes only uniqueness among all abstract poset isomorphisms, not necessarily the author's intended canonical meaning of 'à isom unique près'. Argument: Define M with objects A,B; Hom(A,A) = {id_A}, Hom(B,B) = {id_B}, Hom(A,B) = {f,g} with f distinct from g, and Hom(B,A) empty. Identity compositions define all possible composites and satisfy the category axioms. The identities are monic. To test either f or g for monicity, each set Hom(X,A) has at most one member, so any parallel arrows into A are equal before composition. The only endomorphisms are identities. All arrows into B are f, g, id_B. The first two define distinct subobjects because their only possible domain automorphism is id_A; neither is equivalent to id_B because A and B are not isomorphic. Both lie below [id_B]. If [f] <= [g], a factorization would require f = g composed with h for h:A -> A, forcing h = id_A and f = g, a contradiction; the reverse comparison is equally impossible. Thus Sub(B) has exactly two incomparable elements [f],[g] below one greatest element. Swapping [f] and [g] and fixing [id_B] is a nonidentity order automorphism. The canonical transport induced by id_B is instead the identity.
